title: Iowa's 1st Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Iowa's 1st Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks against Democratic challenger Christina Bohannan in a third consecutive rematch. The district covers 20 counties in southeastern Iowa, including Iowa City, Davenport, Muscatine, and Burlington, and is rated a 'toss up' by the Cook Political Report with a Partisan Voting Index of R+4. Miller-Meeks, an ophthalmologist and U.S. Army veteran first elected in 2020, won her 2024 race by just 799 votes after a recount. Bohannan, a University of Iowa law professor and former state representative, argues the district is ready for change on issues including healthcare costs, tariffs, and Medicaid funding.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the 2026 general election in Iowa's 1st Congressional District were found as of this writing. The race is rated 'Toss Up' by nonpartisan forecasters including Cook Political Report.

candidates.name: Mariannette Miller-Meeks
candidates.summary: Mariannette Miller-Meeks is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Iowa's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2020. She is an ophthalmologist, a 24-year U.S. Army veteran (private to lieutenant colonel), and former director of the Iowa Department of Public Health. Miller-Meeks won her 2024 reelection by 799 votes after a recount and secured the 2026 Republican primary with 71.6% of the vote.

candidates.name: Christina Bohannan
candidates.summary: Christina Bohannan is a University of Iowa law professor, former Iowa state representative, and the Democratic nominee for Iowa's 1st Congressional District. She defeated incumbent state Rep. Vicki Lensing in the 2020 primary and served one term in the Iowa House (2021-2023). Bohannan previously ran for this congressional seat in 2022 and 2024, losing both times to Miller-Meeks by narrow margins. She won the 2026 Democratic primary with 81.5% of the vote and campaigns on lowering healthcare costs, opposing Trump's tariff policies, and ethics reform.

forecast.rationale: No public district-specific 2026 general-election polling is available, so confidence is low. Nonpartisan race context rates this as a Toss Up — Cook Political Report — indicating no clear favorite. The district has a modest Republican structural lean (R+4), and incumbent Mariannette Miller-Meeks has won three times, but her 2024 victory came by only 799 votes after a recount. Democrat Christina Bohannan is a repeat challenger who has kept both of her previous races extremely close. The very slight Republican edge (53%) reflects incumbency and the district's partisan baseline, but the margin of victory is likely to be razor-thin again, consistent with a true tossup.
